title: zazzle run use cases
description: Running a build or test through `zazzle run`.

entities.name: Run a build or test with cleaned output
entities.description: A coding agent runs its project's build or tests through `zazzle run` and reads only what matters from the output.
entities.goal: Learn whether a build or test passed, and why not, from a short answer with the command's exit code.
preconditions: zazzle and zazzled are installed side by side (or ZAZZLE_DAEMON names zazzled), or zazzled is run directly as `zazzled wrap`.
The command exists in the caller's environment.
postconditions: The agent has the cleaned output and the footer on standard output, tagged `[r:ID]` when it was stored for read-again.
The exit status is the command's own, so a failing command still fails.

flow.action: Runs `zazzle run -- cargo test` (or another build, test or install command) in its shell; the invoker replaces itself with `zazzled wrap -- cargo test`.
Reads its options up to `--` or the first argument that is not one; the rest is the command.
Starts the command with standard output and error on one pipe, collects up to 64 MiB, and waits for it to exit or for the timeout.
Tidies the output, applies the detected or named profile, runs clean's steps within the budget and adds the footer.

Stores the result with the raw output when there is an output store, tagging it with its id and, when anything was dropped or cut, a read-again --full hint; prints it and exits with the command's exit code.

alternatives.condition: No command, an unknown option or profile, or a bad number.
alternatives.outcome: `zazzled: ...` on standard error, exit 2; nothing is run.
It is killed; the footer says so and the exit status is 124.

alternatives.condition: No profile matches the command, --profile none is given, or --lossless is set.
alternatives.outcome: Only clean's steps (lossless ones with --lossless) and the budget apply.
